record.original_question: Describe all chiral polytopes of nearly full rank.

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Describe all chiral polytopes of nearly full rank.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) of ranks $-1, 0, 1, \dots, n$ satisfy the standard combinatorial axioms of an abstract polytope: it has a unique minimum face of rank $-1$ and a unique maximum face of rank $n$, every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly one face of each rank, the poset is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition (for any two faces $F < G$ with $\operatorname{rank}(G) - \operatorname{rank}(F) = 2$, there are exactly two faces strictly between $F$ and $G$).

Let $\mathcal{P}$ be such a polytope. Its automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts on the set of flags. The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is called regular if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts transitively on flags. It is called chiral if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ has exactly two orbits on flags such that any two adjacent flags (flags differing in exactly one face) lie in different orbits.

A faithful (geometric) realization of $\mathcal{P}$ in Euclidean $d$-space $\mathbb{E}^d$ assigns to each face of $\mathcal{P}$ a subset of $\mathbb{E}^d$, compatibly with the partial order, in such a way that the symmetry group of the realized figure is isomorphic (via the realization) to $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ and acts in the same way on flags. The realization has full rank if its ambient dimension equals $n$ when $\mathcal{P}$ is finite, or $n-1$ when $\mathcal{P}$ is infinite (an apeirotope). It is said to have nearly full rank if its ambient dimension equals $n+1$ in the finite case, or $n$ in the infinite case.

Problem. Describe (classify up to similarity) all chiral abstract polytopes and apeirotopes admitting a faithful realization of nearly full rank in Euclidean space.
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous classification for regular polytopes and apeirotopes of nearly full rank has been completed (work of McMullen and collaborators). For the chiral case, related questions have seen recent progress (e.g., chiral polytopes of full rank exist only in ranks 4 and 5, established by Cunningham–Pellicer and others around 2020–2021), but a full classification of chiral polytopes of nearly full rank does not appear in the literature found, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Chiral polytopes of full rank exist only in ranks 4 and 5
status_evidence.snippet: A chiral polytope of full rank can only have rank 4 or 5.
status_evidence.claim: The full-rank case of the analogous chiral classification has only recently been settled, indicating the nearly-full-rank case is more recent/open.

status_evidence.title: A chiral 5-polytope of full rank
status_evidence.snippet: The first known chiral 5-polytope of full rank was presented.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on chiral polytopes of constrained ambient dimension; classification at nearly full rank is not stated.

status_evidence.title: Regular polytopes of nearly full rank
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of regular polytopes of nearly full rank by McMullen.
status_evidence.claim: The regular analogue is classified, providing context that the chiral version is the natural next problem.
